# Power station size for a fridge during an outage

**Short answer:** For a typical full-size fridge, get a pure sine wave power station with at least 1,300 W of surge output. Plan on about 1,000 Wh to cover most of a day, or about 2,000 Wh for 1.5 days. Check surge first, because it blocks more fridges than battery size does.

## The three checks

1. **Continuous watts:** A full-size fridge runs at roughly 100-250 W, so almost any 1,000 W-class station clears this ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)).
2. **Surge watts:** The compressor spikes at startup. Sources put it at 1,000-1,200 W for a typical fridge and up to 2,400 W for large or older units. Look for a surge rating of 1,300 W or more, and 2,400 W if yours is a big side-by-side or an older model ([HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/), [BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)). A station that is too small will trip at the first start, however big its battery is ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)).
3. **Watt-hours:** The compressor cycles on and off, so average draw is far below the label wattage. Estimates vary by source:
   - About 41 W average for an 18 cu ft ENERGY STAR model, which works out to roughly 1,400 Wh per day once you add inverter losses and 20% headroom ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)).
   - About 50-70 W average in other guides ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)).

For your own fridge, take the kWh/year figure on the EnergyGuide label, multiply by 1,000, divide by 8,760 to get average watts, then multiply by 24 hours and your outage days. Divide that by 0.85 for inverter losses and add about 20% headroom ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)). A plug-in energy meter gives a more accurate number ([iTechGuides](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-size-a-portable-power-station-for-a-refrigerator-and-essential-devices/)).

## Rough runtimes (35% duty cycle, 150 W running)

| Capacity | Approx. runtime |
|---|---|
| ~1,000 Wh | 16-17 hours |
| ~1,500 Wh | ~25 hours |
| ~2,000 Wh | ~33 hours |

These figures are from [HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/). Real runtime will be shorter with a hot kitchen, frequent door openings, or extra devices on the station.

## Picks by outage length

- **Up to about 12-17 hours:** The [BLUETTI AC180](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage) (1,152 Wh, 1,800 W, 2,700 W peak, about $399-699) or the [Jackery Explorer 1000 v2](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage) (about $449-799). Both pass the surge check for most fridges.
- **24-36 hours:** The [BLUETTI AC200L](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l) has 2,048 Wh, 2,400 W continuous, and a 3,600 W surge. It expands up to 8,192 Wh and is $899 at BLUETTI's store. One site reports its code AFF5OFF takes $44.95 off, but check at checkout. That link is an affiliate link, so the merchant pays the site a commission at no cost to you. The [Anker SOLIX S2000](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator) (2,010 Wh, 1,500 W, 3,000 W peak) is another option. That link goes to Anker's sizing guide, which features the S2000.
- **Multi-day outages:** You'll need 4,000 Wh or more, or an expandable unit with solar.

## Tips

- Keep the fridge door shut. The USDA says food is unsafe after 4 hours above 40°F with the door closed ([HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)).
- Make sure the station has a pure sine wave inverter, since modified sine wave can make compressors run hot or fail to start.
- Add up any other devices you want to run, like a router or lights, and size for the total.

If you tell me your fridge's size or EnergyGuide kWh/year, and how long an outage you want to cover, I can narrow this to one or two specific models.
